newsitem.title: GERMANY: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest - May 14.
newsitem.headline: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest - May 14.

text.p: REUTERS GERMAN ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the German press on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

BONN - German newspapers and magazines lost ground in advertising income to television and direct mailing in 1996, Germany's central advertising association says. While mass media as a whole posted a mild 3.1 percent gain in advertising income last year, an increasingly cut-throat market did not allow all to share the wealth equally, the ZAW says. It predicts 2.4 percent growth for 1997. (Reuter)

BONN - Television channels in Germany saw modest gains in advertising income in 1996 but public broadcasters' sales idled, the ZAW says. The German television industry posted a relatively weak 8.7 percent rate of growth in 1996 to 6.9 billion marks ($4 billion) after several boom years. (Reuter)
BONN - Germany again landed in third place among the top national advertising markets, behind the United States and Japan. (Reuter)
FRANKFURT - Advertising volume for regional newspapers dropped 8.6 percent in the first quarter of 1997, compared to the same period in the previous year. (Horizont)
FRANKFURT - Swiss creative agency Weber Hodel Schmid (WHS) has won the account for the debut of the MCC-Auto Smart mini car. (Horizont)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:
FRANKFURT - The computer industry in German posted record turnover last year, growing by 14 percent to 1.7 billion marks. (Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung)
FUERTH - Electronics group Grundig wins contract from British pay television service BSkyB to build digital set top decoder boxes. (Reuter)
FRANKFURT - The number of German companies offering products or services on the Internet is expected to increase to nearly 150,000 by the end of this year to 58,000. (Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung)
BERLIN - Publishing group Axel Spring Verlag posts net profits of 163.8 million marks for 1996, up from 142 million the previous year and expects further earnings and imporvement in 1997. (Reuter)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

BONN - Telecommunications giant Deutsche Telekom reports strong profits for 1996 and says earnings will more than double this year as the company girds for a full-scale assault on its home market by new competitors. At its first results news conference since Europe's largest ever flotation six months ago, Telekom set out to show that it is matching ambitious forecasts made during months of road shows to woo investors. (Reuter)

BONN - The German government is considering selling some of its stake in Deutsche Telekom this year, sources in the ruling coalition say. The sources are confirming the tenor of a report in the business daily Handelsblatt which said Finance Minister Theo Waigel wanted to sell some of the government's biggest holding this year to ease budget problems. (Reuter)

FRANKFURT - German specialty chemicals and consumer goods group Henkel KGaA forecasts strong full year results after several high-profile acquiisitions last year helped fuel first quarter business. (Reuter)

BONN - The government aims to maintain investment incentives to ex-communist east Germany at current levels, but stopped short of giving the plan its final approval, a spokesman says. A new plan by Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt would allocate 5.7 billion marks in investment bonuses annually to the region for six years from 1999, and create an extra 2,800 training places there, spokesman Peter Hausmann says. (Reuter)
WIESBADEN - The Federal Statistics Office reports that April wholesale prices rose 0.2 from the previous month. (Reuter)
